title: HB331 (136th Legislature (2025-2026)): Remove firearm mufflers, suppressors as dangerous ordnance

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Ohio) (gun-policy Stage 5, Ohio); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Ohio text (As Introduced (00_IN), ; official copy, https://search-prod.lis.state.oh.us/api/v2/general_assembly_136/legislation/hb331/00_IN/pdf/ (Open States text id 90137469))
provenance.note: As introduced. Struck: 'Any firearm muffler or suppressor' from the dangerous-ordnance definition (division (K)(5), old (K)(6) renumbered); the clause requiring authorization under state/federal law and NFA registration in R.C. 1533.04(A) (sentence quoted ends at the strike, a comma in the print); and R.C. 2923.17(C)(8), the hunting exemption for suppressors. 2923.17(A) is unchanged but now no longer reaches suppressors.

operative_text:
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.11(K)(5)): Any combination of parts that is intended by the owner for use in converting any firearm or other device into a dangerous ordnance.
Section 1 (R.C. 1533.04(A)): A person who holds a valid hunting license issued under this chapter and who hunts game birds or wild quadrupeds may use a suppressor attached to a gun that is authorized to be used for hunting by section 1533.16 of the Revised Code while hunting.
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.17(A)): No person shall knowingly acquire, have, carry, or use any dangerous ordnance.
